habitats: Moist pockets along the groundwater-damming dyke
Lower meadow margins with persistent capillary moisture
summary: A multistemmed shrub bearing low clusters of soft, wax-white fruit containing sugar and starch. Its harvest precedes madre_de_agua's principal dry-season crop. Fruiting patches indicate accessible subsurface moisture, while carried fruit and abandoned caches connect feeding to dispersal.

links: Eastern summer drought limits reproductive water
Dyke-retained groundwater sustains selected root zones
Watered shrubs ripen accessible clusters during the seasonal drying transition
chains.play: Harvest ripe fruit for food and gifts; compare productive shrubs with dry meadow.
chains.weakness: Falling groundwater reduces the crop; fog alone cannot sustain it.
observe: Find low fruit beside moist soil.
Return as the meadow begins drying.

plausibility.summary: Fruit production requires persistent root water; its timing is conditional rather than a fixed calendar event.

analogues.mechanism: Animal-accessible fleshy fruit rewards transport of enclosed seeds.

chains.trait: Pale waxy berries, ripe scent and small hard seeds
links: Pale fruit contrasts with green leaves in available daylight
Ripe volatiles persist locally in sheltered, still dawn air
Rondo carry fruit to caches; swallowed seeds receive additional dispersal
Only surviving seeds in moist microsites recruit
chains.play: Follow fruit-carrying rondo, offer sound berries, and revisit abandoned caches after rain.
chains.weakness: Wind disrupts scent trails; damaged fruit spoils and many cached seeds are eaten.
observe: Compare intact and bruised fallen fruit.
Find seedlings at an abandoned moist cache.

plausibility.summary: Fruit reflects light without glowing. Dispersal provides opportunities, not guaranteed germination or universal gut survival.

analogues.mechanism: Aromatic soft pulp surrounds small hard seeds dispersed by fruit consumers; rondo caching is an additional fictional interaction.

poison.signal: Plain green foliage; wax-white ripe fruit.

gameplay.notes: Fruit supports befriending rondo and receptive zanco; zanco courtship remains dance-based. Spoiled berries lose gift value.

relations.note: Carried fruit and abandoned caches move viable seeds.
Browses reachable ripe clusters; some swallowed seeds survive.
Consumes fruit and carries gift clusters.
Overlapping roots compete for wet soil and light.
Uses the same groundwater reservoir through independent roots.

generator.trunk: Three to seven grey-brown woody stems; thin persistent fruit calyces.

overlay_rules: Bruised fallen fruit browns; no emission.

placement.slope: Gentle footslopes and sheltered dyke pockets
placement.fog: Frequent dawn fog; no irrigation guarantee

generator.seasonal: Flowers before the drying transition; fruit timing follows water availability. Each berry encloses one or two small seeds.
generator.wind_response: Flexible stems bend; clusters chiefly 0.3–1 m high remain partly sheltered.

journal.en: White berries scent the dawn. The herd carries some away; a few return as bushes.
journal.es: Las bayas blancas perfuman el alba. La manada se lleva algunas; unas pocas vuelven hechas arbustos.

observe: Follow a rondo carrying pale fruit.
Compare productive moist patches with dry margins.
Offer ripe fruit and revisit abandoned caches.
secrets: A moist abandoned cache can establish a new patch after rain.
